The overall experience at this restaurant was very disappointing. The service was extremely poor and slow, and the staff was not polite or professional in their behavior.

featured_reviews.name: J G Irani
featured_reviews.review_text:
Food and friends make the best memories. So true! These are created at Dadar Darbar.
Dadar Darbar the most happening food and beverage restaurant set in a train dining car right outside Dadar East Station is a must visit for Mumbaikars and people travelling to Mumbai. Dadar Darbar is an affordable value for money, no frills, full on service, conveniently located restaurant. Dadar Darbar serves you North Indian menu with a twist. They create and cook up a fusion of indian, regional and international tastes for different palates.
For starters we had kheema paav, chicken lollypop, surmai fry, chicken spring roll. Whereas Hyderabadi chicken biryani was fulfilling as the main dish. For deserts we had Afghani dryfruits ice cream, Caramel custard and the Arabic pudding.
At Dadar Darbar, good food creates good mood!

featured_reviews.name: Prodipto Goswami
featured_reviews.review_text: An amazing experience. Right next to the entrance of Dadar E, this quaint, in-a-bogie, restaurant serves excellent food. Nice ambience with lovely light music.  The service is prompt and with a smile. Thank you Indian Railways...and whoever their contractor is who runs this!

featured_reviews.name: viraj s wadkar
featured_reviews.review_text:
Dadar Darbar is a lifesaver for late-night travelers! The best part is that it’s open the whole night, so if you miss your last local train, this place feels like a cozy train compartment just a few steps from the station – literally next door!

The restaurant maintains good hygiene, which is a big plus, and the staff is polite. Service can be a little slow when it’s crowded, but that’s understandable. The food taste really surprised me – much better than expected!

If you’ve had a long train journey and need good food without traveling any further, this is the perfect spot. Convenient, clean, and satisfying late-night cravings right near the station!

featured_reviews.name: Huzefa Rangwala
featured_reviews.review_text:
It’s a nice theme to have a restaurant in an old train compartment. Gives a different feel. Apart from the looks the food is actually good. It really tastes good. It’s not a fine dine restaurant so don’t expect amazing service but it was a good experience.
Since it is just outside the station, it is convenient if you have just arrived and are hungry. It’s affordable too, not too expensive.

featured_reviews.name: Namrata Gaikwad.
featured_reviews.review_text:
Dadar Darbar in Dadar East has become one of our go to places, and for good reason. We’ve visited many times, and the experience has consistently been wonderful. The food is genuinely delicious, rich in flavor, well prepared, and always satisfying. Whether it’s a quick meal or a relaxed outing, the quality never disappoints. What truly makes the place stand out is the service. The staff is polite, attentive, and always ready to help with a smile. A special mention goes to Mr. Irshad, who has attended our table on multiple occasions. His service is exceptional courteous, prompt, and very thoughtful. He makes sure everything is just right, which adds a personal touch to the entire dining experience.
The ambiance is comfortable and welcoming, making it a great spot for family visits as well as casual dining. Overall, Dadar Darbar offers a perfect combination of tasty food, great service, and a friendly atmosphere. We always look forward to coming back and would highly recommend it to anyone looking for a satisfying meal in Dadar East.

featured_reviews.name: vijay wadia
featured_reviews.review_text:
Biryani Barbeque Chinese restaurant is a multi cuisine restaurant in Borivali West.
One of the oldest restaurants.
It offers vegetarian and non vegetarian food.
It has good options for non vegetarian Biryani, Chicken tikka, mutton Sikh kabab, tandoori chicken.
It has a good variety of Chinese dishes.
Food quality is good and all the dishes are tasty.
This restaurant has ample seating arrangements on the ground floor and first floor. The ambience is ok.
Service is fast enough.
Generally it is a bit crowded during weekends, but the waiting period is manageable as it has more sitting arrangements on the first floor.
It has valet parking so parking is not an issue.
This restaurant also serves alcohol.
Offers a variety of Indian and imported whisky, Vodka, rum, Gin and liquor. Also has a good choice of beers.
The food prices are ok, but alcohol is on a bit higher side.
Overall it is worth visiting with family and value for money.

featured_reviews.name: Hitesh
featured_reviews.review_text:
I had a satisfying experience at Restro Bar - Biryani Barbeque. The place offers a comfortable dining environment and is well-suited for a relaxed meal with friends or family.

What stands out is that it is one of the few places in Borivali West that serves good quality non-vegetarian food. Given that the area has a significant Gujarati community and is largely dominated by vegetarian options, this restaurant provides a refreshing and much-needed alternative for non-vegetarian diners.

The food was well-prepared, flavourful, and lived up to expectations. The biryani and barbeque items were particularly enjoyable, with balanced spices and good portion sizes. The service was prompt and courteous, contributing positively to the overall experience.

Overall, it is a dependable choice for those looking for good non-vegetarian options in Borivali West, and I would certainly recommend it for a satisfying meal.

The service was attentive and friendly, with staff who genuinely seemed to care about our experience, making us feel well looked after from start to finish. The food was excellent, showcasing fresh ingredients and carefully balanced flavors, and each dish was presented beautifully. Any BBC u visit is thd best in all senses, my always go to place and have a great time with family. I had serving of Mutton Biryani, a celebrated and aromatic rice dish that originated on the Indian subcontinent. The vibrant yellow and orange hues of the rice come from saffron or food coloring, while the garnish of crispy fried onions adds a distinct texture and flavor. Borivali Biryani Centre is a go-to spot for biryani lovers who crave rich flavors and hearty portions. This casual eatery has a straightforward, no-frills vibe — all attention is on delivering satisfying, flavorful meals.

The biryanis here are aromatic, perfectly spiced, and generously portioned, making them a hit with both regulars and first-time visitors. Beyond biryani, the menu also includes other popular North Indian dishes that complement the main attraction.

Service is friendly and efficient, and the place is ideal for a quick lunch, dinner, or takeaway. Borivali Biryani Centre is the kind of spot where you know you’ll get consistent, comforting flavors every time — perfect for a satisfying, casual meal.

featured_reviews.name: Anup More
featured_reviews.review_text: We went there in a group of four people and it was suggested by my friend as a popular eat out and the restaurant is the oldest or the main branch. We ordered Paya soup & Tulsi tomato soup for starters and both were amazing. The soups were right in taste, not too mild not too spicy. For appetizers we ordered hara bhara kebab & mutton seekh kebab, again, both were amazing. In the main course we went ahead with Veg & Chicken Dum Biryani, the biryanis were okay. As we were three people eating chicken biryani, we ordered full chicken biryani which was sufficient if you want to eat right else you go for a large size which would serve 4 people. Lastly we had custard pudding and blue mist as desserts and coolers. The pudding was very good. Overall, a very good place to visit for food, I can go again for Paya soup, mutton seekh kebab and custard pudding.

This is a restaurant 🏨 chain ⛓️ in Mumbai, known for its Mughlai 🍢 and non-veg food. I won't recommend this place much if you are Jain 👳or pure vegetarian 🥬. It's a 2 florey restaurant with AC 🌬️ and Non-AC 🪭 section usually the restaurant is packed during weekend. The name of the restaurant is BBC (Borivali Biryani 🍚 Center) known for its Biryani and majorly non-veg. If talking about the staff 🧑‍💼 they were occupied a lot and a bit ignorant about the customer 🙂, I asked 3-4 times for the same thing to different people still could not get much respond. The ambience ✨ of of Family restaurant and cleanliness 🧹 is maintained. Washroom is unisex and 🫧 clean however there was water blocked at some place.

Further, talking about the foods and the drinks that we tried :

1. Blue bliss - it's basically a lemonade 🍋 with an added food colour 🔵, it was sweet but an good option from the mocktail menu.

2. Virgin mojito 🍸- Just an old school taste of soda 🥤mixed with lemon 🧃 juice and with some basil 🌿 leafs in it.

3. Lemon Iced Tea ☕- It's a cool starter in drinks 🍷 to go with along with some heavy food.

3. Veg dum biryani 🌾- It's a simple option if you don't want to explore kuch and it's a safer option. I asked them to make it a bit spicy 🔥. A taste of mixed vegetables 🍆 and paneer served with boondi raita.

4. Paneer Crispy Plum  - It's a chinese sweet🍯 starter with some added veggies. I usually don't prefer sweets so I won't recommend the same.

5. Mushroom  🍄 Tikka - It's just like paneer tikka 🍢 but instead paneer mushroom 🍄 is used. For a change you can try mushrooms instead of Paneer.

The overall experience was okay as the staff was not attentive, the food taste in veg was not that good and I didn't have much to explore on the menu. You can go here for mughlai and kebabs dish 🍽️.

featured_reviews.name: Vinit Vinayak
featured_reviews.review_text:
I recently visited Muthuswamy Cafe, and it was an amazing experience for anyone who loves authentic South Indian food.

The place has a simple yet comforting vibe, and the aroma itself sets the mood as soon as you walk in. The food is absolutely top-notch—fresh, flavorful, and perfectly balanced. From crispy dosas to soft idlis and rich sambhar, everything tasted authentic and satisfying.

The service was quick and efficient, and the staff was polite and attentive throughout. It’s one of those places where you go for the food and end up loving the whole experience.

If you’re in Dadar and craving real South Indian flavors, this spot is definitely worth visiting!

featured_reviews.name: Himanshi Patel
featured_reviews.review_text: Café Muthuswami in Dadar is a cozy spot that brings authentic South Indian flavors to life. Known for its crispy dosas, soft idlis, and rich, aromatic filter coffee, every bite feels comforting and nostalgic. The ambiance is simple yet inviting, perfect for casual catch-ups or a relaxed solo meal. Service is quick, and the food quality is consistently impressive. Whether you’re craving a hearty breakfast or a light evening snack, this café delivers on both taste and experience. A must-visit for anyone who loves traditional South Indian food in Mumbai with a homely touch and great value.

featured_reviews.name: Pooja Fulsundar
featured_reviews.review_text:
Mutuswami Cafe is located just outside Dadar East railway station, so it’s very easy to find and perfect for a quick stop after travel. They have both indoor and outdoor seating, which is nice if you want to sit comfortably or just grab something quickly.
We tried the strawberry milkshake & mango milkshake both were thick, chilled, and refreshing. The paper masala dosa was big, crispy, and came with good chutney and sambar. Kanchipuram idli was soft and flavourful, a little different from regular idli and worth trying.
Cheese tava rice was spicy, cheesy, and filling good if you’re very hungry. We ended with pineapple sheera, which was warm, slightly sweet, and had a nice fruity taste.
Overall, it’s a good place for South Indian food and quick snacks near the station.

featured_reviews.name: VISHAL UPADHYAY
featured_reviews.review_text: We ordered cheese pav bhaji, and masala dosa and both were extremely delicious. We loved both the items. Cost wise it appeared a little costly given the ambience, and quality of service. It was situated near Dadar railway station and is fine for some snacking.

featured_reviews.name: Gayatri
featured_reviews.review_text:
If you’re in Dadar and craving authentic South Indian flavors any time of the day, Muttuswami Cafe is the place to be!
This is the only café in the area open 24/7, making it a perfect spot for early breakfasts, late-night cravings, or casual meetups at any hour.
The food quality is outstanding, with every dish served fresh, flavorful, and satisfying:
Cheese Pav Bhaji – perfectly buttery with a generous layer of melted cheese that elevates the classic taste.
Podi Idli – soft, bite-sized idlis coated beautifully in spicy podi masala and ghee.
Muttuswami Special Benne Dosa – rich, crispy, and soaked in butter with a delicious traditional touch.
Spring Dosa – a unique fusion twist, crispy outside with a flavorful stuffed filling inside.
Fruit Custard Dessert – creamy, refreshing, and loaded with fresh fruits for the perfect sweet ending.
Their fresh juices are equally impressive — especially the pomegranate juice and the orange-mosambi mix, both refreshing and naturally sweet.
What truly makes the experience special is the warm and polite staff. The service is quick, attentive, and always delivered with a smile. The beautiful interiors create a clean, cozy, and welcoming atmosphere, making you want to sit back and enjoy your meal.

featured_reviews.name: imran khan
featured_reviews.review_text:
This place is located very near to Dadar East railway station... AC dining room. But the space is very small. Outdoor sitting area is spacious but one cannot sit there during daytime.
Food was amazing tasty. A little higher price.. people may feel for this .. however if you compare to food outlets in the mall .. it's the same. Combos one can have .. quantity fulfills  the hunger for one person. Overall nice experience. Recommended if around Dadar railway station.

featured_reviews.name: Taran Arora
featured_reviews.review_text: If you enjoy South Indian food and want a cleaner, more café-style experience in Dadar, Mutuswami is worth trying. Best dishes to order are Benne dosa, thatte idli, rasam rice , filter coffee and pineapple sheera.  Staff is very courteous and welcoming.

featured_reviews.name: Mithil Thakker

They have indoor and outdoor seating. Post 8 pm it's a busy schedule for the restaurant so go a bit early to get the best available table of the house.

Our food recommendations.

Podi Idli:
You have to visit this place to experience this extraordinary delicacy of the house .

Benne Masala Dosa:
This one won't disappoint you if you are fond of benne then definitely give this a try.

Pav Bhaji:
Again a house supremacy. Spicy and Tangy burst of flavours with every bite .

The Mango Milkshake was rich and thick  . Even their cold coffee has a supreme vibe.

Pineapple Sheera .
When at a South Indian cuisine specialist restaurant then you can't miss this legendary dish . Indeed a heavenly experience.

Overall a delightful experience as always.

Happy and Safe Fooding Until Next Time.

And they even added the cost of a cold drink that we had brought from home without asking us. You can see it clearly on the bill—it has been written with a pen....From today onwards, I have decided never to come here again. My family and people from my society will also not visit BBC anymore. I am not provoking anyone; I am just saying that if you go there, please be careful about hygiene.
If that hair had gone into someone’s lungs, what could have happened? The hotel staff does not seem to care. What was even more surprising was that when I informed the hotel seniors (higher authority) about the issue, they themselves said, “You must have put the hair in the food. featured_reviews.review_text:
Tried out Borivali Biryani Centre recently and honestly – if you’re a biryani lover, this place should be on your list!

We had their Chicken Tikka Dum Biryani and it was amazing. The flavors were spot on – smoky, spicy, and super satisfying. We also tried the Jahangir Tikka, and it was perfectly grilled with just the right amount of spice. Really juicy and flavorful – definitely worth a try.

To sip on, we ordered a mojito, which was alright – refreshing but nothing extraordinary.

Now here’s the thing – the biryanis here steal the show. If you’re visiting, go for the biryanis. That’s where they truly shine. Other stuff’s okay, but nothing comes close to their signature biryani.

A heads-up though: the place gets really crowded. There’s usually a long queue outside, so if you’re planning a visit, try to go early or see if you can reserve a table. We had to call the staff multiple times just to place an order, and while they were polite, they seemed short-staffed for the kind of crowd they handle.

On the plus side, the ambiance is nice and fresh, and the restaurant has a clean, cozy vibe.

Final verdict:

Come for the biryani. Be patient with the service. Totally worth it if you’re craving something flavorful and filling. Would recommend, just plan your timing!

★★★☆☆ 3.5/5 – Convenient & Affordable Dining Near Dadar Station

Shapoor Restaurant – Dadar East, Mumbai

Located just a short walk from Dadar Railway Station (East), Shapoor Restaurant is a no-frills, casual dining spot offering a mix of North Indian, Chinese, and Mughlai cuisine.

What I Liked:

Convenient Location: Right near Dadar East station—ideal for a quick meal or casual dine-in before/after your commute.

Variety of Cuisine: A good mix of North Indian and Chinese. I tried their Butter Chicken and found it flavorful and well-prepared.

Affordable Pricing: Budget-friendly rates make it great for everyday meals.

Prompt Service: Even during busy hours, food was served without long delays.

What Could Be Better:

Ambiance: Clean but very basic. Don’t expect a fancy setting—more functional than aesthetic.

Small Portions for Extras: Items like extra sambar with Udid Wada felt limited.

Some Inconsistencies (as per reviews): While my experience was smooth, online reviews mention occasional issues like undercooked rice or delayed service.

Overall:

If you’re looking for a quick, filling, and affordable meal near Dadar, Shapoor is a solid choice. It’s not a place for ambiance lovers or fine dining seekers, but it gets the job done for everyday comfort food.

Recommended for: Office-goers, travelers, and locals looking for casual dining.

featured_reviews.name: ADESH PATANKAR (NUSTA TRAVEL)
featured_reviews.review_text:
A Perfect Family Treat: Review of Farmhouse, Borivali
If you are looking for a dining spot in Borivali that balances quality food with a pocket-friendly budget, Farmhouse is a fantastic choice. I recently visited this restaurant with my family, and it turned out to be a delightful experience that I would highly recommend to locals and visitors alike.

The Highlights
Food (4/5): The menu is diverse, offering a great mix of North Indian, Chinese, and Continental dishes. We found the flavors to be authentic and the portions quite generous. Whether you are a fan of their signature tandoori starters or their sizzling main courses, the quality is consistent and satisfying.

Ambiance (4/5): The restaurant boasts a very inviting and well-decorated interior. It strikes a nice balance between urban elegance and a cozy, rustic charm, making it an ideal setting for a relaxed family dinner.

Vibes (3.5/5): The atmosphere is generally lively and warm. While the "vibe" is solid, it can get quite busy during peak hours, which adds to the energy but might feel a bit crowded for those looking for a quieter meal.

Value for Money: One of the best parts about Farmhouse is the pricing. For a family outing, it is incredibly reasonable—you can easily enjoy a full meal for around ₹1,200 for two people, which is rare for a restaurant of this caliber.

Overall Rating: ⭐⭐⭐⭐ (4/5)
With its great food and beautiful setting, Farmhouse Borivali is a top-tier option for a budget-friendly family feast.

featured_reviews.name: vishwa oza
featured_reviews.review_text:
Another day, another Instagram feed restaurant.Blabber all day proved, yet again, that the cafés we see on Reels are likely paying people to promote a product that is not worthy of its price tag. The reality here is far more disappointing and genuinely annoying.
SEATING ARRANGEMENT: The Advance Booking Penalty (0/5)
We were a group of five, spending a total of ₹2,831. We specifically reserved seats through Zomato and paid a ₹500 advance to ensure a good experience.
In return, we were given the most uncomfortable, low-slung seats imaginable. The table was awkwardly low compared to the chairs, making it impossible to eat comfortably.
0/5 Rating for giving such a terrible seating arrangement even after an advance booking. You penalize your paying customers for reserving!
FOOD: Looks vs. Reality (Pocket Breaking & Tasteless)
The food looks tempting for a photo, but the moment you taste it, the high cost feels like a pocket-breaking insult. Everything was severely lacking in flavor and quality.
1. Thai Basil Cottage Cheese Bau (₹545 for 3 piece):
Dry, Tasteless Disaster. The paneer stuffing was decent but dry. The outer layer (which I assume was maida) was tasteless and super dry.
It desperately needed a sauce. They served us a microscopic cup of Schezwan sauce when asked. Seriously?
2. Burrata Pizza (₹830 for 6 slice):
The Most Bland Pizza Ever. The Burrata cheese tasted exactly like makhan (homemade butter) Indian moms skim off while making ghee.
Never imagine a pizza could taste this bad while charging ₹830. Respect to Dominos and Eva's Pizza—you deliver actual, good pizza.
3. Mango Matcha Latte (₹475 for one small glass):
HORRIBLE. You ruined matcha. I was excited for my friend to try matcha for the first time, and this concoction was an absolute offense.
Believe me, people, matcha tastes better than this. You need to drastically improve this recipe.
4. Pomegranate POP (₹395 for one glass):
A Flat, Overpriced Joke. It was essentially just soda, over-squeezed lemon, and a faint hint of pomegranate. No sugar, no flavor, just disappointment.
5. Peri Peri Fries (₹275):
The ONLY redeemable item. Of course, we had to spend ₹275 for a small bowl of fries, but at least they were hot, seasoned, and actually tasted right.
Conclusion - The Instagram Trap
Overall, the food was not good and severely overpriced. The ambience is achaa (good), of course—it’s only there for the show/visuals.
It seems like your rent is too high, and you are charging customers for low-quality, low-quantity food to cover your costs.
Another day of regretting selecting a restaurant from an Instagram Reel. 👎 Save your money!
